metadata.proof: SOURCE: Multipart file upload POST to /validator/uploads. SINK: allowed_file() at lines 36-38 only checks the file extension after the last dot, with no MIME-type inspection, no magic-byte/content sniffing, and no file-size limit. An attacker can upload a file named 'shell.php.png' or 'evil.js.html' — both pass the extension check since the suffix is in the allowlist. Critically, 'html' is in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS, so a file named 'phish.html' passes validation and is saved to uploads/. Combined with the /validator/getXML endpoint (which serves files with Content-Type: text/html), this enables stored-XSS and phishing payloads.
